survey: A spiral topiary of four stacked leafy tiers, getting smaller toward a pointed leafy tip. It sits in soil inside a round planter made of rounded stone blocks, and the planter stands on a terracotta paved path that curves around it. Behind it are lawn, a wooden bench, a potted flower, a lamp post, a hedge and sky. The camera is a moderately high three-quarter view looking down. The planter rim is an open ellipse, with block tops visible all the way round. The front blocks show their full face. The blocks at the sides narrow and turn with the curve, and the back blocks are short and seen across the soil. The bottom edge of the foliage, where it meets the soil, curves upward at the sides like the rim, so the topiary agrees with the same downward view. The seams between tiers run diagonally, which reads as the spiral wrapping around the form, not as a mismatched horizon. The paving stones get smaller and more foreshortened toward the back and follow the path's curve. The bench seat and armrest tops are visible a little, consistent with the slightly elevated eye level and the hedge line behind. The planter sits flat on the paving at the angle the ground is drawn.
